She reports longstanding patterns of similar behavior since childhood, with onset prior to age 12, though formal evaluation was not previously pursued.

Current symptoms include frequent motor restlessness, such as persistent hand and foot movements and difficulty remaining seated during meetings or structured activities where sitting is expected. She is described as having difficulty engaging in calm, low-stimulation leisure activities and tends to choose or transform activities into highly active pursuits. Observers note that she appears continuously active, as if driven by an internal sense of urgency, with difficulty slowing down.

In interpersonal contexts, she speaks at length and at a rapid pace, often dominating conversations. She has recurrent difficulty waiting for others to finish speaking and regularly interjects or overlaps others’ speech, and she may intrude into ongoing conversations or group activities without appropriate hesitation. These symptoms have resulted in workplace feedback regarding her behavior during staff meetings and challenges maintaining appropriate boundaries in collaborative settings.
D003_l022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Delusional Disorder
